CURRENCY-STALENESS CORRECTION (2026-08-25, [specialist], citation-integrity follow-up, per [specialist] flag): the deposit route is legally fixed in IDR, not USD; the commonly-quoted "USD 130,000" figure is stale, implying a rate near 15,385 IDR/USD (roughly where the rupiah sat at this visa's 2024 launch). At Bank Indonesia's own official rate as of 2026-08-24 (buy 17,616.47 / sell 17,793.53, midpoint ~17,705 IDR/USD — bi.go.id, primary-institutional), IDR 2B converts to ~$112,970, about 13% lower than $130,000. Since the legal bar is IDR-fixed, rupiah depreciation has made this route CHEAPER in USD terms over 2024-2026, not more expensive — the opposite direction from what a stale higher-USD figure implies. Any USD figure for this threshold should be treated as a point-in-time estimate, not the authoritative value; the IDR figure is authoritative.

Trajectory set to "not yet assessed" pending a source that actually assesses the rhythm, rather than carrying over the dropped framing

fact_label: Territorial-tax facility for new foreign tax residents (first 4 years)
value_raw: Qualifying foreign nationals (must meet certain skill/expertise requirements) who become Indonesian tax residents are taxed only on Indonesian-sourced income (even if paid offshore) for their first 4 years as a tax resident; standard worldwide-income taxation applies after that window, or for anyone who doesn't qualify for the facility at all
notes: Landed 2026-07-18 ([specialist]), filling the Income viability criterion's zero-fact gap. A genuinely undocumented-until-now structural fact for this project: unlike Panama/Costa Rica/Georgia-style territorial systems, Indonesia's territorial treatment is temporary (4 years) and conditional (skill-requirement-gated), not a standing feature — worth naming precisely rather than reading Indonesia as a territorial-tax country outright. Eligibility skill-requirement criteria themselves not independently pulled to a primary source — PwC's own phrasing ("certain skill requirements") not further decomposed. Re-verified against raw page content 2026-08-24 ([specialist]), citation-integrity review: page confirms foreign new tax residents "can be taxed only on Indonesian-sourced income" and that this runs for the first four years, contingent on skill requirements and absent an overriding tax treaty — claim holds

value_raw: A foreign national becomes an Indonesian tax resident at 183 cumulative days present within any 12-month period, or on day 1 with documented intent to remain; presence under ~120 days generally means tax applies only to Indonesian-sourced income
notes: Cross-checked against PwC Tax Summaries (taxsummaries.pwc.com) the same session — anyone actually living in Bali full-time (the realistic shape of this project's own relocation scenario) crosses this threshold within their first year, making the territorial-facility row above and the worldwide-taxation row below directly load-bearing, not academic

fact_label: Worldwide-income taxation, progressive brackets (post-facility or non-qualifying resident)
value_raw: 0% to IDR 54M; 5% IDR 54-60M; 15% IDR 60-250M; 25% IDR 250-500M; 30% IDR 500M-5B; 35% above IDR 5B (annual)
notes: At the June 2026 rupiah rate (~18,100 IDR/USD, see the currency-crisis row above), brackets convert to roughly: 0% to ~$2,980; 5% to ~$3,310; 15% to ~$13,800; 25% to ~$27,600; 30% to ~$276,000; 35% above that. This is the rate structure that applies once the 4-year territorial facility lapses (or to any resident who never qualified for it) — a real, dated compounding fact worth reading alongside the Second Home Visa's own 3-year permanent-residency (PR) conversion clock, which lands almost the same point on the calendar as this facility's own 4-year cutoff

fact_label: On-location income archetype — no supporting legal route found
value_raw: No route found (Second Home Visa, E33G, and Retirement KITAS all structurally exclude local Indonesian-client income or local employment)
notes: A genuine cross-archetype income-viability fact in its own right, not just a visa-mechanics footnote — restated here as its own discrete row per the 2026-07-18 thinnest-criteria fill pass. Every realistic route this project has found for Bali is foreign-income-only by design

fact_label: UNESCO Cultural Landscape of Bali Province (Subak System)
value_raw: Inscribed 2012-07-06; ~19,519 ha across 5 sites incl. Catur Angga Batukaru (Jatiluwih, 17,376 ha), Lake Batur (1,606 ha), Pakerisan river watershed (529 ha, oldest known irrigation system in Bali), and two royal water temples; the subak irrigation philosophy dates to the 9th century
notes: Landed 2026-07-18 ([specialist]), filling the Nature & water-adjacency criterion's zero-fact gap. UNESCO inscription itself is a primary-institutional-adjacent fact (whc.unesco.org attempted, 404'd; Wikipedia's own account cites the 36th World Heritage Committee session directly)

value_raw: Separated from Bali mainland by the Badung Strait; major dive/snorkel sites incl. Batu Lumbung (Manta Point), Batu Meling, Batu Abah, Toya Pakeh, Malibu Point; December 2024 discovery of a ~4,000m² Galaxea astreata coral colony, one of the largest known; 41 villages maintain a bird-sanctuary agreement since 2006
notes: Landed 2026-07-18 ([specialist]). Not a formally-designated marine protected area in the strict legal sense — the bird sanctuary is a village-level traditional-regulation agreement (awig-awig), not a national conservation designation; worth stating precisely rather than implying formal MPA status

value_raw: Protects native species including the critically endangered Bali myna (Bali starling)
notes: Landed 2026-07-18 ([specialist]). Diving sites Tulamben, Amed, and Menjangan Island (within/adjacent to this park) also named as coral-reef/marine-life destinations by the same source, not independently detailed further

fact_label: Water-resource over-extraction by the tourism industry
value_raw: Over-exploitation by the tourist industry has caused 200 of Bali's ~400 rivers to run dry
notes: Landed 2026-07-18 ([specialist]) as part of the mandatory positive-lever-hunt discipline applied in reverse: the original 2026-07-11 pass stated "no countervailing water-quality or access issue found" for the criterion's 5/5 score — this is a real, sourced, currently-live countervailing fact that pass didn't have. Original Wikipedia source for this specific figure not independently re-traced to its own primary citation — single-sourced to the Wikipedia aggregation itself, flagged accordingly. Re-verified against raw page content 2026-08-24 ([specialist]), citation-integrity review: page states "Over-exploitation by the tourist industry has led to 200 out of 400 rivers on the island drying up" — figure confirmed present and matching

value_raw: Recurring annual monsoon-season plastic/trash washup onto Bali's beaches (incl. Kuta); a 2017 "garbage emergency" was declared after a 3.6-mile stretch of coastline was covered in plastic waste, the same year Bali received ~5.7 million tourists; a major government beach cleanup was launched 2026-02-03 following presidential criticism of the ongoing waste problem
notes: Landed 2026-07-18 ([specialist]). Cross-corroborated across the Wikipedia Bali and Kuta,_Bali articles independently. A real, recurring, seasonal (not one-off) countervailing fact against the "tropical paradise" framing — worth reading alongside the water-overextraction row above as one compounding environmental-strain picture, not isolated incidents. Re-verified against raw page content 2026-08-24 ([specialist]), citation-integrity review: page confirms the 2017 "garbage emergency" during a "nearly 5.7 million tourists" year, the 3.6-mile plastic-covered coastline, and a beach cleanup launched "on 3 February 2026" after President Prabowo's criticism — all four sub-claims confirmed present and matching
Landed 2026-07-18 ([specialist]). One named example, not confirmed representative of Bali's coastline generally — flagged as a single-location data point, not extrapolated to other beaches

fact_label: Uluwatu/Bukit traffic congestion — government engineering response
value_raw: Chronic congestion in the Pecatu-Uluwatu tourism corridor; a traffic-flow restriction system (turn restrictions across 6 intersections, enforced 5-10pm daily) trialed June 2026 was made permanent by Badung Regency's Transportation Agency as of July 2026
notes: Landed 2026-07-18 ([specialist]), filling the Routine sustainability/pace-of-life criterion's zero-fact gap. A real, current, government-acknowledged congestion problem serious enough to trigger a formal regulatory response — read alongside the enforcement-crackdown finding as a second, independent driver of day-to-day friction distinct from immigration enforcement itself

value_raw: Not a new 2026 phenomenon: a 2017 "garbage emergency" occurred during a ~5.7-million-visitor year; Bali was already planning a US$10 tourist tax as of 2020; 2026 saw an active government beach-cleanup crisis response — a real, multi-year worsening pattern, not a one-off event
notes: Landed 2026-07-18 ([specialist]). Read this together with the water-overextraction and beach-plastic-pollution rows homed under Nature & water-adjacency above — same underlying visitor-volume driver, split across two criteria because one is about the natural draw itself and the other is about daily-life friction from crowding/infrastructure strain, per this project's own criterion boundaries. CORRECTED 2026-08-24 ([specialist]), citation-integrity review: source_url was misattributed to Wikipedia's Overtourism article — re-read against raw content, that page's only Bali mention is "Bali was, in 2020, planning a US$10 tourist tax," with no mention of the 2017 garbage emergency or the 5.7-million-visitor figure. Those two sub-claims are actually confirmed on the Wikipedia Bali article instead (same page already cited for the water-overextraction and beach-plastic-pollution rows above) — source_url corrected to point there. The 2020 US$10-tourist-tax detail remains additionally corroborated on the Overtourism article specifically, just not as this row's primary citation

fact_label: Restricted-nationality list — calling visa (multi-agency security-vetted pre-approval, excl. Israel — see its own dedicated row)
value_raw: AF, KP, LR, NG, SO
date: 2024-2025 (monitoring procedures finalized, per Middle East Monitor citing CNBC Indonesia)
notes: Extracted 2026-07-22 ([specialist]), same harvest. Indonesia's 'calling visa' (visa lapor diri) is its most restrictive ordinary entry category, reserved for 6 nationalities: Afghanistan, Israel, Liberia, Nigeria, North Korea, Somalia. Israel deliberately split OUT of this list into its own dedicated fact row (ID:entry-restriction-israel-no-diplomatic-relations, below) because its own restriction rests on a materially different, more specific rationale (no diplomatic relations, not a generic high-risk-security screen) and carries its own document_conditional_note disclosure the other 5 don't share -- same split-out precedent Morocco's Ukraine/Venezuela rows already established in this project when treatment genuinely differs within one nominal list. Entry for all 6 nationalities permitted only via Soekarno-Hatta (Jakarta) or I Gusti Ngurah Rai (Bali) airports; reviewed by a multi-agency coordination team (immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, intelligence/BAIS, police, military); prior Directorate General of Immigration (Jakarta) approval required before a visa application can be filed; processing weeks to months. Cross-corroborated: embassyinformation.com, visa-indonesia.com's dedicated calling-visa guide, Middle East Monitor (citing CNBC Indonesia immigration-intelligence data). No day-count figure found common to all 5 remaining nationalities -- entry_max_days left unmapped/null rather than guessed. imigrasi.go.id/evisa.imigrasi.go.id both HTTP 403. Spot-checked 2026-08-25 ([specialist], verification review): Afghanistan/North Korea/Somalia/Liberia/Nigeria all independently confirmed present on the underlying Wikipedia page via direct fetch.

fact_label: Entry restriction — Israel (no diplomatic relations, calling visa)
value_raw: IL
document_conditional_note: Indonesia has no diplomatic relations with Israel. Entry requires prior approval from the Directorate General of Immigration in Jakarta plus a multi-agency 'calling visa' review (immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, intelligence/BAIS, police, military); permitted only via Soekarno-Hatta (Jakarta) or I Gusti Ngurah Rai (Bali) airports. Practically severe, not merely bureaucratic: only 51 calling visas were issued to Israeli nationals in the ~11 months through 2025-11-30 (immigration-intelligence data via CNBC Indonesia/Middle East Monitor) -- a near-total practical bar for ordinary tourism, though not a formal legal suspension. No religious-tourism or pilgrimage carve-out found.
notes: PRIORITY row, a direct catch (2026-07-21 late night) -- real gap, not previously captured anywhere in this project's own research (our records 0 hits, Indonesia/*.md 0 hits before). A named scope seam, not a research failure: [specialist] 2026-07-11 first pass never covered nationality rules at all; [specialist] 2026-07-16 Israeli-passport pass was deliberately scoped to the 10 then-active candidates, Indonesia outside that set (her own honest flag at the time). Indonesia has no diplomatic relations with Israel. Israeli passport holders sit on the same 'calling visa' list as Afghanistan/Liberia/Nigeria/North Korea/Somalia (ID:restricted-nationality-list-calling-visa-tier), split into this own dedicated row because the practical reality goes further than the shared list entry and rests on a distinct rationale (diplomatic non-relations, not a generic security screen): Indonesia's own immigration-intelligence data (via CNBC Indonesia, reported by Middle East Monitor 2026-01-08) shows only 51 calling visas issued to Israeli nationals in the ~11 months through 2025-11-30 -- Israel ranked 4th among calling-visa recipient nationalities, behind Nigeria, Somalia, Afghanistan. Stated approved purposes: business discussions, purchases, exhibitions, meetings, tourism, private visits by elderly travelers. Checked directly and found NONE: no religious-tourism or pilgrimage carve-out for Israeli nationals specifically -- a real checked-and-absent result, not silence. Tier call, named as a doubt: rendered visa-required rather than suspended -- entry is not a formal legal suspension (unlike the US's Proclamation 10998 partial suspension of Venezuelan entry, this project's other suspended-tier precedent; a visa can genuinely be obtained, people do get through), so suspended would overstate the legal mechanism; but bare visa-required alone would understate the real barrier that token implies elsewhere in this table (51 approvals over ~11 months against ~9.7M Israelis is a near-total practical bar for ordinary tourism). This entry's severity is disclosed in a companion note rather than the headline tier alone -- a genuine judgment call about how to represent a practical bar that falls short of a formal legal suspension, flagged for specialist review rather than treated as settled. Cross-corroborated: embassyinformation.com, middleeastmonitor.com (2026-01-08, citing CNBC Indonesia), visa-indonesia.com's calling-visa guide, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_policy_of_Indonesia. imigrasi.go.id/evisa.imigrasi.go.id both HTTP 403 -- aggregator-recheck tier, not primary-institutional.
